criteria.description: Correctly verifies R^T R = I for R (orthonormal columns).
Correctly computes det(R')=-1 and identifies it as a reflection, explaining why orthonormality alone doesn't guarantee a rotation.

solutions.fullSolution:
R's columns (0,1,0),(-1,0,0),(0,0,1) are mutually orthogonal and unit length, so R^T R = I. det(R) = 1 (cofactor expansion along row 3, which has a single 1 in the bottom-right, gives det=1*det([[0,-1],[1,0]])=1*(0-(-1))=1).
R' has the same orthonormal columns (sign flip in one entry doesn't change orthogonality/unit length), so R'^T R'=I still. But det(R') = -1 (the sign flip in the (3,3) entry flips the determinant's sign). R' is an orthonormal matrix but represents a reflection, not a rotation: SO(3) requires BOTH orthonormality AND det=+1, since orthonormality alone (the orthogonal group O(3)) includes both rotations and reflections.

criteria.description: Correctly differentiates x(t)=R(t)x_body to get xdot=Rdot*x_body.
Correctly substitutes the geometric definition wxx(t)=skew(w)R(t)x_body.
Correctly argues that equality for an arbitrary x_body implies equality of the matrices themselves, Rdot=skew(w)R.

commonErrors: Only verifying the identity for one specific x_body rather than arguing it must hold for the matrices themselves since x_body is arbitrary.

solutions.fullSolution:
x(t) = R(t)*x_body, x_body constant, so xdot(t) = Rdot(t)*x_body.
Geometric definition: xdot(t) = w x x(t) = skew(w)*x(t) = skew(w)*R(t)*x_body.
Setting both expressions for xdot(t) equal: Rdot(t)*x_body = skew(w)*R(t)*x_body. Since x_body is an ARBITRARY fixed vector in R^3 (any body point), this equality of the two sides applied to every possible x_body forces the two matrices multiplying x_body to be equal themselves: Rdot(t) = skew(w)*R(t).
